subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should OpenClaw implement `workspaceAccess: "none"` as a writable isolated `/workspace` while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted and preserving read-only skill/bind protections?
rationale: The desired direction has maintainer signal, but the implementation changes a sandbox write boundary across Docker/OpenShell mounts, local and remote filesystem bridges, and tool exposure, so automation should not choose the permanent guardrails alone.

options.title: Implement Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Make only the sandbox-owned workspace writable under `none`, keep the real workspace hidden, and require full bridge/tool/docs/tests plus live proof before closing.

options.title: Keep Strict No-Write None
options.body: Leave `none` fail-closed, update docs and tool exposure to match, and treat writable isolated workspaces as not planned.

options.title: Split Custom Binds Separately
options.body: Fix isolated `/workspace` here and keep explicit host `:rw` bind authorization scoped to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Implement Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Make only the sandbox-owned workspace writable under `none`, keep the real workspace hidden, and require full bridge/tool/docs/tests plus live proof before closing.
